t: Bishop Notger (972–1008) turned the see of Liège into a territorial principality of the Holy Roman Empire.
The Peace of Fexhe of 1316 bound the prince-bishop to change the law only with the consent of the estates.
Coal and arms making made it rich; the Liège Revolution of 1789 and French annexation in 1795 ended it.
dyk: The Feast of Corpus Christi began in Liège, instituted by its bishop in 1246 after the visions of Juliana of Cornillon, before Pope Urban IV extended it to the whole church.
ev: Otto III grants Bishop Notger the county of Huy
Liège buys Bouillon from Godfrey of Bouillon
The Feast of Corpus Christi is first instituted in Liège
The Peace of Fexhe establishes government with the consent of the estates
John the Fearless defeats the Liège rebels at Othée
Charles the Bold sacks and burns Liège
The Liège Revolution drives out the prince-bishop
